supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:46 UTC, ivy.chen launched PowerShell from Explorer to compress \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; the archive file was created at 13:39:50 UTC.
At 13:45:32 UTC, ivy.chen launched Chrome to quickshare-drop.net.
Chrome, running as ivy.chen, connected through the proxy to quickshare-drop.net; the proxy recorded about 51 MB client-to-server and 8.8 KB server-to-client over the tunnel.

The archive of client files shortly preceded a large outbound transfer to a file-sharing destination that is not among the services approved in the supplied inventory. Together, these facts strongly support suspected data exfiltration and a malicious disposition for the alerted activity.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy and connection records provide tunnel metadata and byte counts, but do not show the encrypted tunnel's contents.
The evidence does not directly establish that c.zip was the payload transferred, or identify the specific files or data included in the transfer.
claims_not_established: Whether c.zip, or any particular client files, were uploaded in the alerted transfer.
The sensitivity of the archived data, whether the transfer was authorized, or the user's intent.
Whether the destination received or retained the transferred data.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine WS-ICHEN-01, including c.zip, its creation metadata, size, hash, and relevant file-access history.
Obtain any available proxy inspection or destination-side records that could identify the uploaded object, account, or upload result.
Verify with the data owner and ivy.chen whether the archive and transfer were authorized; preserve relevant browser history and user activity.
unrelated_findings: Cisco AnyConnect's UI was launched on WS-ICHEN-01. The supplied environment context says there is no VPN; review this separately, without treating it as evidence for the alerted transfer. Records: T039-00190, T039-00192.
